subject: Follow-up: Foundry pricing, token velocity, and startup discount request
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@foundry.ai>, Connor Lee <connor@foundry.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Foundry pricing, token velocity, and startup discount request

Hi Olivia / Connor —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re all aligned:

What we heard
- You expect peak inference demand around 45–60M tokens/month once search and assist are in prod.
- A large chunk (~40%) is short-form queries (<= 64 tokens); long-tail prompts average ~420 tokens.
- Initial budget target for inference is in the range $30k–$50k/month for 1H GA, with an ambition to scale.

Immediate asks from you
1) Clarify pricing math for committed discounts (what does $/1M tokens look like at different commit bands).
2) Confirm eligibility for the Startup Program + founder credit (Foundry is Series A, < $10M ARR).
3) Get a simple run-rate projection we can drop into finance (example: 50M tokens/month => $X/month at proposed tier).

What I’ll do by EOD tomorrow
- Share a compact pricing worksheet with 3 commitment scenarios (trial, 6mo commit, 12mo commit) and per-1M token target rates. Attachment: baseline-token-estimates.xlsx
- Note startup program options and the founder sponsorship path.
- Flag any engineering constraints (latency/kv-cache) that change cost profile.

Attachments: foundry-demo-notes.pdf (demo highlights), baseline-token-estimates.xlsx (ballpark math)

If this summary looks right, I’ll route an initial discount ask to Ben for approval and include Marissa from the sales ops side for contract/term details.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first LLM inference
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@foundry.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor Lee <connor@foundry.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Foundry pricing, token velocity, and startup discount request

Thanks, Mina — this is great and matches our notes. A couple of quick clarifications: 

- The 45–60M tokens is our conservative projection for Q2 post-launch; we could see spikes to ~90M for a week during marketing pushes.
- Budget: we have runway to commit to ~$25k/month today but need to understand what a 6–12 month commitment buys us in unit price.
- Startup program: Foundry closed Series A last month (~$7.6M) — qualifies, right? Would founder credit apply to the first invoice only or be spread?

Also, Connor asked if you can show a target $/1M tokens at the level of $600, $900, $1,200 so we can compare to internal TCO models.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

-Olivia
Head of Product, Foundry

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@foundry.ai>, Connor Lee <connor@foundry.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Foundry pricing, token velocity, and startup discount request

Olivia — thanks for the clarity. Short answers before I loop in Ben/Marissa formally: 

- Yes, Foundry qualifies for our Startup Program (Series A, < $15M ARR). Founder credit is typically applied to the first invoice as a one-time credit, but we can discuss spreading it across the first 2 invoices if helpful for cashflow.

- Attached spreadsheet has three commitment scenarios (Trial: 0 commit, 6mo: 25M/mo commit, 12mo: 50M/mo commit) and the corresponding unit economics. High-level snapshot: 
  • Trial (no commit): list $/1M tokens = $1,250
  • 6mo commit (25M/mo): discounted $/1M tokens ≈ $925
  • 12mo commit (50M/mo): discounted $/1M tokens ≈ $680

- Given your stated target band, hitting ~$600 / 1M would require a multi-year structure or a top-tier committed band + rebate. We can map a 24mo multi-year proposal if you want that target.

Next steps I’m proposing:
1) I’ll ask Ben to greenlight a preliminary 12mo pricing proposal with a founder credit applied to invoice 1 and a mechanistic rebate if you exceed the commit by >20% in any month.
2) Marissa can prepare a short term-sheet (non-binding) to capture commit bands and SLAs.
3) Connor — if you can confirm which commit band (25M vs 50M) looks more feasible for CFO sign-off, we’ll model total spend and present a clean number to finance.

Looping in Ben and Marissa now.

Best,
Mina

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Olivia Barnes <olivia@foundry.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Foundry pricing, token velocity, and startup discount request

Thanks for the context, team. Quick internal note (copied to prospect for transparency):

- Mina: the 12mo / 50M band at ~$680 / 1M is within approval for a standard startup package + founder credit. I’ll approve a one-time founder credit up to $10k applied to the first invoice.
- To reach the ~$600 / 1M target Olivia asked about, we can explore a 24mo structure with an annualized commit escalation and a small performance rebate (arrangement would require legal review). I don’t expect legal to push back on the concept but timeline is ~7–10 business days for contract language.
- Marissa: please draft a short non-binding term-sheet reflecting: 6mo/25M @ $925/1M; 12mo/50M @ $680/1M w/ $10k founder credit on invoice 1; optional 24mo exploratory path to $600/1M with rebate. Link to draft in HubSpot + Drive.

Olivia — happy to join a call with finance / legal if that helps expedite. If Foundry can confirm whether CFO prefers a 6mo or 12mo starting structure, we’ll prioritize the right paperwork.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
